promise: Every external process HangarCore or the `hangar` command starts has a deadline it cannot outlive: HangarCore through ProcessRunner, and `hangar --exec` through its own loop, which signals the process group so a wrapped command cannot outlive it.
why: Was scoped to HangarCore alone, and went green over the spawn in hangar-cli, which is the riskiest in the repo because the program is whatever the user typed after --exec. The killpg half exists because terminate() and kill() reach the direct child only: `sh -c 'trap "" TERM; sleep 25'` left the grandchild running while the deadline reported it had finished. Deliberately not widened to all of app/Sources: Updates.swift and Uninstaller.swift also start processes, under the updater's own gates, and this case has never checked them. Blessing them by widening a grep would be a claim nobody made.
command: ! grep -rln 'Process()' app/Sources/HangarCore app/Sources/hangar-cli --include='*.swift' | grep -qvE 'ProcessRunner.swift|main.swift' && grep -q 'killpg(entry.process.processIdentifier, SIGTERM)' app/Sources/hangar-cli/main.swift && grep -q 'killpg(entry.process.processIdentifier, SIGKILL)' app/Sources/hangar-cli/main.swift
